To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the risk of conjunctiva scarring in tracoma is associated with the HLA ligand of KIR, and is exacerbated by heterozygosity at 2DL2/2DL3.
the odds of scarring increased with increasing number of genome copies for HLA-C2 and that this effect was further enhanced by KIR2DL/KIR2DL2 heterozygosity.
HLA-C and KIR2DS2/KIR2DS3/KIR2DS4/KIR2DL2/3 genotypes are associated with conjunctival disease in trachoma.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the genetic basis of conjunctival inflammation in trachoma, a disease caused by infection with the intracellular bacterium C. trachomatis.
the innate response to chlamydial infections and the genetic basis of disease susceptibility and severity.
the genetic control of the human immune response and its consequences for disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the HLA-C2 ligand of KIR2DL and the presence of KIR2DS1, KIR2DS4 and/or KIR2DS5 in the presence of KRL2DL2 and/or KIR 2DL3 is associated with conjunctival pathology in trachoma.

the HLA-C2 ligands of KIR2DL1, KIR2DL4 and KIR2DS4 are risk factors for trachomatous conjunctival scaring and that the risk is increased in individuals who also carry the HLA-C ligands of K2DL2/K2DL3.
HLA-C is a risk factor for conjunctival scaring and that KIR heterozygosity at 2DL2/2DL3 increases this risk.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
KIR2DS1/KIR2DL2 homozygotes and HLA-C2/C2 homozygous individuals are at the highest risk of conjunctiva scarring in trichoma.
the HLA-C ligand of KIR, which is the most important determinant of the KIR repertoire, is a risk factor for conjunctival scaring in trachoma.
HLA-C and KIR2DS3/KIR2DL2/3 polymorphisms interact to increase the risk of trachomatously scarring conjunctiva in individuals infected with C. trachomatis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
HLA-C is a major genetic risk factor for the development of conjunctival scar in trachoma.
the HLA-C ligand of KIR is a major genetic determinant of conjunctival fibrosis in trachoma.
HLA class I genotypes are a major risk factor for trachomatous conjunctival scaring and that KIR genotypes may exacerbate this risk.
